newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended broadly higher and toward the top of the day's range in light volume Wednesday, buoyed by a late-session bout of local short covering, trading sources said.
Most-active May rose $13 per tonne on the day, to $1,280, having traded from $1,281 to $1,268. Spot March closed up $10, to $1,235, while the outer months gained $9 to $13.
Volume was estimated at 3,966 lots, down from Tuesday's official tally of 4,435 lots.

A drop in the value of the U.S. dollar versus the British pound touched off some arbitrage interest early in the session, as operators favored the New York market over sterling-denominated London cocoa. London futures ended flat to weaker on Tuesday, with active May closing at 880 stg, unchanged on the day.
Dealers also noted light speculative buying, but said scale-up selling by the trade capped gains.

Technically, traders said May's close above a gap filled today between $1,273 and $1,277 was viewed as constructive. But they said May would need to get by $1,291 and $1,300 to attract substantial buying interest. On the downside, near-term May support was seen at $1,262-$1,264, followed by its contract low of $1,252 set last week.
